agent_output.affected_group: Automobile manufacturers (NAICS 336111 Automobile Manufacturing and 336112 Light Truck and Utility Vehicle Manufacturing) subject to NHTSA corporate average fuel economy (CAFE) standards that fall short of compliance and cannot cover the shortfall with credits
agent_output.change_summary: NHTSA final rule repeals the January 14, 2021 interim final rule (which had delayed the inflation-adjusted CAFE civil penalty rate until Model Year 2022) and reverts to the December 2016 final rule, so the adjusted $14 per 0.1 mpg rate applies beginning with Model Year 2019 (MY 2019-2021), with the statutorily required annual adjustment raising the rate to $15 for 2022; the pre-2019 rate remains $5.50. The rule also codifies in 49 CFR 578.6(h)(3) an inflation-adjusted cap of $29 per 0.1 mpg. Effective May 31, 2022; petitions for reconsideration due May 16, 2022.

evidence.quote:
NHTSA is repealing the 
interim final rule and reverting to the December 2016 final rule that 
would apply the adjustment for the CAFE civil penalty rate beginning 
with Model Year 2019. In this rule, NHTSA is also applying the 
statutorily required annual adjustments through 2022.

Therefore, NHTSA is codifying 
the civil penalty rate of $15, along with clarifying regulatory text 
explaining that the civil penalty rate is $14 for MY 2019 through MY 
2021 (and $5.50 for MYs before 2019).

Therefore, NHTSA is codifying 
the cap at $29, and NHTSA will make subsequent annual adjustments as 
required.

This action is expected to 
affect manufacturers of motor

[[Page 19005]]

vehicles. Specifically, this action affects manufacturers from NAICS 
codes 336111--Automobile Manufacturing, and 336112--Light Truck and 
Utility Vehicle Manufacturing, which both have a small business size 
standard threshold of 1,500 employees.

assesses civil penalties against manufacturers that 
violate applicable standards and are unable to make up the shortfall 
with credits.

Effective date: This rule is effective as May 31, 2022.
    Petitions for reconsideration: Petitions for reconsideration of 
this final rule must be received not later than May 16, 2022.

uncertainties: Final rule published 2022-04-01 with future effective date 2022-05-31; the document states the Second Circuit twice held the December 2016 rule to be in force, so practical novelty of the MY 2019-2021 rate is contested within the source; clearly new elements are the $15 rate for 2022 and the $29 cap.
Effective date text contains a typo ('effective as May 31, 2022').
Event type could alternatively be new_legal_requirement.
Interim final rule subject to consolidated Second Circuit litigation in abeyance; petitions for reconsideration due May 16, 2022.
Model-year application dates are not calendar effective dates.
GPO text contains a Cloudflare-obfuscated email placeholder in FOR FURTHER INFORMATION CONTACT.
